bio: A great-grandson of Ali ibn Abi Talib who served as governor of Medina under the Abbasid caliph al-Mansur. He accepted Abbasid rule, unlike many Alids, and married his daughter to the first Abbasid caliph al-Saffah; he later fell out with al-Mansur, who removed him and confiscated his wealth, which al-Mahdi afterwards restored. He died on the road to Mecca in 783 and was buried at al-Hajir.

bio: A Medinan narrator of the ninth generation known as al-Shajari. He was blind and said to accept prompting in narration; Ibn Hajar graded him da'if (weak), as did al-Dhahabi and Abu Hatim, and al-Saji noted anomalies in his hadith. He was the father of the narrator Ibrahim bin Yahya.
research_evidence: يحيى بن محمد بن عباد بن هانئ، المدني، الشجري، الهنائي — التاسعة — death year 200 AH (matches our 9th-generation record; our record has no death year)

bio: A Medinan narrator of the seventh generation known as al-Farisi al-Kharrat, whose given name was Subayh according to Ibn Ma'in and al-Bukhari, or Humayd according to others. Ibn Ma'in and Ibn Hajar graded him trustworthy and Ibn Hibban listed him in al-Thiqat; his death is placed between 151 and 160 AH. He transmitted Abu Hurayra's reports via Abu Salih Dhakwan.
research_evidence: أبو المليح: صبيح، قاله ابن معين والبخاري، وقيل: حميد — الفارسي، المدني، الخراط — السابعة (7th generation; death placed 151-160 AH; our record has no death year)
dod_s: c. 777 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

bio: A Meccan narrator who transmitted from 'Ata bin Abi Rabah. Critics differed on him: Abu Hatim did not praise his narrations and one scholar deemed him majhul (unknown), while Ibn Hibban counted him among the trustworthy.
research_evidence: Ayyub ibn Thabit al-Makki — أيوب بن ثابت المكي, Makka (no death year stated on the page or in our record; identified by exact full name, Meccan nisba, and narrator role; page lists his generation as 6th where our record says 7th)
dod_s: c. 777 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

bio: A Meccan Qurashi narrator. Al-Bukhari described him as munkar al-hadith and Abu Hatim said he erred beyond the limit of acceptability; a single narration of his, concerning dyeing with henna, was recorded by Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah.

bio: A Basran narrator nicknamed al-Saffi because he kept to the first row (saff) of the congregational prayer in the mosque for fifty years. Ibn Hibban counted him among the trustworthy, and al-Nasa'i recorded a narration of his.

bio: A Basran Tamimi narrator known as Abu Bishr al-Muzalliq, a neighbour of Hammad bin Zayd. Some scholars said he was 'not strong'; al-Nasa'i recorded a single narration of his, from 'A'isha, concerning the Prophet's fragrance.

dod_s: c. 777 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

bio: A Basran narrator of the seventh generation known as al-'Attar (the perfumer). Ibn Hajar rated him salih al-hadith and al-Dhahabi called him saduq; Ibn 'Adi said 'he is truthful in my view, for I have not seen a munkar narration of his.' His death is placed between 171 and 180 AH.

bio: A Basran narrator of the Bahila tribe who transmitted from Ziyad al-Numayri. Hadith critics were severe on him: 'Ali ibn al-Madini said he narrated rejected reports, and al-Bukhari declared him munkar al-hadith.

bio: A narrator of the eighth generation associated with Basra and Baghdad who transmitted from his father Zayd ibn al-Hawari al-'Ammi. Hadith critics rejected him: Abu Hatim called him matruk al-hadith (abandoned), and Yahya ibn Ma'in said 'laysa bi-shay' (worthless).
